title: Cubical lattice evaluation represents the normalized derived counit
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], let $r\geq0$, and put $D=\mathbf Z^r$, $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_R$ and $\mathcal E=\mathcal A_R(D)$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Write $t:\mathcal M\to\mathcal E$ for trivial action and $\Gamma$ for invariants [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Use ordinary derived categories and localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For equivariant cochain complexes use the finite Koszul complex of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] and its total $K(P)^n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}K_R(P^b;T)^a$, with differential $d_K+(-1)^a d_P$. Use the specific $\lambda$ computed on injectives in [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-injective-normalization] and the cubical complex, augmentation and evaluation $L,\varepsilon,E_P$ in [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-augmentation-evaluation]. Use the normalized derived adjunction $D(t)\dashv R\Gamma$ and tensor conventions of [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor]. Write $e_P:D(t)R\Gamma(P)\to P$ for its counit. Then for every bounded-below $P$ the actual derived morphisms satisfy
$$Q(E_P)\circ Q(1\otimes\varepsilon)^{-1}=e_P\circ D(t)(\lambda_P):D(t)(QK(P))\longrightarrow P.$$
On every bounded-below termwise injective $J$, the normalized identification $R\Gamma(J)=Q\Gamma(J)$ carries $e_J$ to the localization of the ordinary invariant inclusion $t\Gamma(J)\to J$. Both $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal E$ are closed monoidal Grothendieck abelian categories with functorial flat resolutions; the internal-to-section equivalence and action-site presentation of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison, lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] identify the latter tensor with the diagonal action tensor, whose local restriction is $m\otimes n\mapsto a f^*m\otimes a f^*n$. Trivial action is exact, strong monoidal, left adjoint and preserves flat objects. Its normalized derived tensor comparison on flat-term K-flat representatives is the localization of the ordinary identity comparison $t(X\otimes_R Y)=tX\otimes_R tY$; its unit comparison is localization of the ordinary unit identification. These comparisons are the ones used in the displayed counit formula, so the formula is compatible with tensoring two such counit evaluations. For the regular trivial algebra $R$, the induced right-adjoint cup and unit are $\operatorname{cup}_R$ and the unit of [def-sfb-lattice-algebra-derived-cup]. There is a bridge datum of [def-sfb-lattice-restriction-cup-comparison] (sectionwise-to-ordinary action equivalence, underlying-module and invariant isomorphisms normalized by the invariant inclusions, and the derived bridge normalized on every complex by the computation units) which is compatible: its regular-coefficient derived-invariants isomorphism carries the binary cup and cup unit of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] to $\operatorname{cup}_R$ and that unit.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] for the Grothendieck structures of $\mathcal M,\mathcal E$, exact conservative forgetting $U$, and the normalized adjunction $t\dashv\Gamma$. The internal/section equivalence [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] and the small action-site equivalence [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] present these as categories of module sheaves. Apply [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] and [lem-trf-site-functorial-flat-resolution] on the base site and the action site. Both sites and their rings are small in the fixed coefficient universe, so their module categories have additive closed symmetric tensor and functorial flat resolutions. On the action site a local pure tensor restricts along $(f,a)$ as $a f^*m\otimes a f^*n$. The action-site presentation explicitly identifies sheafification on the action site, after restriction to $(f,1)$, with base-site sheafification carrying its induced action. Apply that clause to the balanced tensor presheaf: its action on pure tensors is diagonal, so its sheafification is the diagonal action tensor. The identity on local pure tensors induces inverse balanced maps by the sheaf tensor universal property. This uses the generated Grothendieck topology of that statement; no composition axiom for its displayed precoverage, or finite limits on the action site, is needed. The tensor unit is $R$ with trivial action. These identifications preserve the associators, unitors and symmetry, whose maps on local generators are the usual rebracketing, scalar multiplication and factor exchange.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the lattice counit and tensor normalization

proof.text: The identity on underlying tensors gives $t(X\otimes_R Y)=tX\otimes_R tY$ and $tR=R$, including all coherence maps. Exactness and the left adjunction are those of [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure]. If $F$ is flat in $\mathcal M$ and $A\to B\to C$ is a short exact sequence in $\mathcal E$, apply the exact forgetful functor $U$. Under the diagonal tensor comparison just established, the underlying tensor sequence with $tF$ is $F\otimes_R UA\to F\otimes_R UB\to F\otimes_R UC$, which is exact by flatness. Since $U$ detects exactness, $tF$ is flat; symmetry gives either tensor order. The identical argument on complexes proves that $tX$ is K-flat whenever $X$ is K-flat: for acyclic $N$ in $\mathcal E$, $U(tX\otimes_R N)=X\otimes_R UN$ is acyclic and $U$ detects acyclicity. Here tensor means the signed direct-sum total, identified by [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the lattice counit and tensor normalization

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction] with $L=t$ and right adjoint $\Gamma$. Its hypotheses hold: the categories are abelian, $t$ is additive exact, and $\mathcal E$ has bounded-below injective resolutions by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure]. Write $\alpha_J:Q\Gamma(J)\to R\Gamma(QJ)$ for the computation unit. The cited counit equation, with the exact termwise comparison suppressed, reads $e_J\circ D(t)(\alpha_J)=Q(\iota_J)$. On bounded-below termwise injective $J$, $\alpha_J$ is invertible by the infrastructure node. Therefore the normalized identification $R\Gamma(J)=Q\Gamma(J)$ makes $e_J=Q(\iota_J)$. The cited adjunction lives on $D^+$; the unbounded adjunction $D(t)\dashv R\Gamma$ of the infrastructure node restricts to $D^+$ (both functors preserve bounded-below objects, $R\Gamma$ being computed on bounded-below injective resolutions), and at targets $QJ$ both hom bijections are the ordinary transpose followed by $\alpha_J$, so the two counits agree on $D^+$, which is all that the item uses. This is the adjunction of [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor]: both derive the same ordinary fixed-section adjunction and use the comparison preserving its computation unit. In particular no change of the counit by an automorphism is allowed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the lattice counit and tensor normalization

proof.text: Put $A_X=1\otimes\varepsilon:tX\otimes_R L\to tX$ and $F_P=Q(E_P)Q(A_{K(P)})^{-1}$. All denominators are quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-augmentation-evaluation]. Let $J$ be bounded below and termwise injective. The same node gives the exact chain-map identity $E_J\circ(tb_J\otimes1)=\iota_J\circ A_{\Gamma J}$. Naturality of augmentation also gives $A_{KJ}\circ(tb_J\otimes1)=tb_J\circ A_{\Gamma J}$. Localize and invert $Q(A_{KJ})$ and $Q(A_{\Gamma J})$. Substitution yields $F_J\circ Q(tb_J)=Q(\iota_J)$. By [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-injective-normalization], $b_J$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $\lambda_J=Q(b_J)^{-1}$ under the injective computation identification. Exactness of $t$ therefore makes $Q(tb_J)$ invertible. Cancellation and step 3 give $F_J=Q(\iota_J)Q(tb_J)^{-1}=e_J\circ D(t)(\lambda_J)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the lattice counit and tensor normalization

proof.text: For bounded-below $P$, take a bounded-below injective resolution $s:P\to J$, supplied by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure]. Make it monomorphic, as [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-injective-normalization] requires: choose injective embeddings $e^n:P^n\hookrightarrow I^n$ (the category is Grothendieck abelian by the same node), let $C^n=I^n\oplus I^{n+1}$ with $d(x,y)=(y,0)$, a bounded-below contractible complex of injectives, and $i^n(p)=(e^np,e^{n+1}dp)$, a termwise monic chain map; replace $s$ by $(s,i):P\to J\oplus C$, still a quasi-isomorphism to a bounded-below termwise injective complex. Naturality of $E$ and $A$ in [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-augmentation-evaluation] gives $Q(s)F_P=F_J D(t)(Q(Ks))$. Naturality of the counit and the normalization equation $\lambda_P=\lambda_J\circ Q(Ks)$ of [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-injective-normalization] give $Q(s)e_PD(t)(\lambda_P)=e_JD(t)(\lambda_J)D(t)(Q(Ks))$. The right sides agree by step 4. Cancel the invertible $Q(s)$ to obtain the displayed formula for $P$. This proves equality of the actual derived morphisms, rather than only equality of their cohomology maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the lattice counit and tensor normalization

proof.text: Apply [lem-derived-right-exact-tensor-comparison] to $t$. Steps 1 and 2 verify its closed braided Grothendieck, flat-resolution, additive, strong monoidal, left-adjoint and flat-preservation hypotheses; exactness implies preservation of quasi-isomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], every termwise image computes the exact derived functor $D(t)$, with its specified localization factorization. Thus $D(t)$ is the exact left-derived presentation, whose cochain computation maps are the termwise identity comparisons. The theorem's normalization then makes the tensor comparison on flat-term K-flat pairs the localization of the ordinary identity comparison. The unit is the localized identity $tR=R$. These are exactly the choices in [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor]. Tensoring the two equalities of step 5 in the derived categories now identifies the tensor of the evaluation roofs, after this tensor comparison, with the tensor of the two normalized counits. This uses the derived tensor of the roofs, computed after K-flat replacement; it does not assert that an arbitrary ordinary tensor of two quasi-isomorphisms is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the lattice counit and tensor normalization

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-lattice-sectionwise-action-bridge] to obtain a bridge datum of [def-sfb-lattice-restriction-cup-comparison]: an exact equivalence $\Phi$ from the sectionwise action category of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] to the ordinary action category of [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor], identity on underlying modules, intertwining trivial actions and diagonal tensors with identity tensor and unit maps, with the invariant isomorphism compatible with the two inclusions and the derived bridge $\beta$ normalized on every complex by the computation units. Hence $\Phi$ carries the sectionwise normalized adjunction (inverse transpose = composition with the inclusion) to that of step 3. By step 3 on the ordinary side and the same computation (the counit equation of [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction] with the invertible computation unit of [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure]) on the sectionwise side, both derived counits at a bounded-below injective $J$ are $Q(\iota_J)$, so $\beta$ matches the counits on $D^+$. Both strong tensor structures on the derived trivial-action functors are the localized identity on flat-term K-flat representatives and the localized identity unit (step 6, and [def-sfb-condensed-action-tensor] with [lem-sfb-condensed-cup-mate-coherence] on the sectionwise side), and $\Phi$ preserves flat-term K-flat complexes because it is the identity on underlying modules and tensors; by the uniqueness in [lem-derived-right-exact-tensor-comparison] they correspond under $\Phi$ and the universe transport.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the lattice counit and tensor normalization

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-condensed-cup-mate-coherence] for the discrete group $D$, the sectionwise lax binary map is uniquely the transpose of $(\varepsilon_A\otimes^{\mathbf L}\varepsilon_B)\circ t$ and its unit the transpose of the regular-unit comparison; this is the cup algebra on $R\Gamma(R[0])$, i.e. the cup and unit of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. By [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor] the ordinary lax map is the mate of the tensor of the two counits with the step-6 tensorator, and [def-sfb-lattice-algebra-derived-cup] defines $\operatorname{cup}_R$ as this map followed by $R\Gamma$ of the localized multiplication $R\otimes R\to R$, which is the identity regular-unit identification, and its unit as the adjunction unit followed by $1_R$. For $A=B=R[0]$ the transposes are taken at the bounded-below target $R[0]$, where the hom bijection is $f\mapsto e_{R}\circ D(t)(f)$. By step 7, $\Phi$ and $\beta$ carry counits, tensorators and regular units to each other, so the two transposes correspond and, by injectivity of the adjunction bijection, the regular-coefficient isomorphism of the bridge carries the restriction-calculus cup and unit to $\operatorname{cup}_R$ and its unit: the bridge datum is compatible. Tensoring two counit evaluations is then compatible with this cup by step 6. At $r=0$, $K$ and the normalized comparisons are identities and the roof is ordinary evaluation, by the cubical and injective-normalization nodes. For the zero ring all module objects and maps are zero, so the equalities hold without an extra hypothesis.
